papers.title: Lymphatic endothelial hemoglobin alpha promotes T cell accumulation and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy during cardiometabolic disease
papers.abstract: Background: Reduction in nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability is postulated to drive the progression of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), such as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. The potent NO scavenger, hemoglobin alpha (Hba), regulates endothelial-derived NO in health and disease. Whether lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) express Hba to modulate NO signaling and promote CMD is unknown. Methods: We generated LEC-specific Hba wildtype and knockout mice and fed them a high fat, high sucrose diet to investigate the role of LEC Hba in CMD progression. To further define the necessity of LEC-derived NO in preventing CMD phenotypes, we generated LEC-specific endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) wildtype and knockout mice and subjected them to normal chow feeding. Results: We found genes encoding Hba were upregulated in the heart during CMD and that Hba was enriched in cardiac lymphatic vessels. Genetic deletion of Hba from LECs prevented CMD-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and reductions in cardiac lymphatic density. Notably, our data demonstrate this occurred independent of changes in the coronary blood vasculature and was driven by local, rather than systemic, changes in NO. Scavenging of NO in vitro increased LEC expression of immunoregulatory genes, aligning with Hba-mediated regulation of immune cell, and more specifically T cell, presence in the heart observed in CMD. Mechanistic studies in vitro revealed modulation of NO around LECs did not impact T cell activation, but instead adhesion ? findings which were validated in vivo. Deletion of eNOS from LECs in otherwise healthy mice recapitulated CMD phenotypes of reduced cardiac lymphatic density, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and T cell enrichment in the heart. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate LEC Hba regulates local NO signaling during CMD to promote cardiac hypertrophic remodeling and inflammation. Thus, disruption of Hba function in LECs poses as a potential therapeutic approach in CMDs associated with reduced NO bioavailability.

papers.title: Acclimation of Dunaliella salina to Olive Mill Wastewater: Oxidative Stress, Genotoxicity and the Role of Light Availability
papers.abstract: Freshwater resources are limited, and their availability is threatened by global climate change. Microalgae-based wastewater treatment enables water recovery for human activities, as microalgae can grow in wastewater while simultaneously removing contaminants within a circular economy framework. An example is OMWW. Thus, we tested the early and prolonged responses to tyrosol, p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, their mixture and 10% OMWW on non-acclimated Dunaliella salina (Chlorophyta), analysing the effects through the DPPH and Comet assays. D. salina exhibited transient physiological damage after 1 day of exposure, whereas no detrimental effects were detected after 8 days, indicating the ability to withstand the toxicity of phenolic compounds and OMWW. Afterwards, we characterised the growth of acclimated D. salina cells to 10% OMWW at 100 and 300 mol photons m-2s-1, analysing the growth rate, pigment content, macromolecular composition and biomass reduction index. We observed that D. salina was able to grow similarly to the control in 10% OMWW when exposed to 300 mol photons m-2s-1, with a similar chla/chlb ratio and carotenoids, a higher amount of proteins and carbohydrates and a more reduced biomass. In conclusion, D. salina demonstrated a high degree of tolerance to OMWW and high acclimatation capability. Moreover, this study indicates that growth of D. salina in OMWW is strongly light-dependent.

papers.title: Dietary betaine-based supplementation improves laying performance and modifies intestinal morphology and microbial profile in hens exposed to a tropical environment
papers.abstract: This study evaluated dietary betaine, alone or combined with vitamin C and/or sodium bicarbonate, in laying hens under chronic tropical heat stress, and characterized the intestinal morphological and microbial responses to the best-performing treatment. Two hundred forty 65-week-old Lohmann Brown hens were allotted to five diets (eight replicates of six birds) for seven weeks: basal diet (T0), betaine (T1), betaine + vitamin C (T2), betaine + sodium bicarbonate (T3), and betaine + sodium bicarbonate + vitamin C (T4). The mean temperature-humidity index was 29.68, indicating severe to very severe heat stress. T3 gave the highest hen-day egg production (89.93%) and egg mass (54.83 g), the lowest feed conversion ratio (1.85), and the lowest overall rectal temperature (41.20 vs. 41.57 Celcius in T0; p < 0.05). T3 was therefore compared with T0 for intestinal histomorphology and microbiota profiling. T3 increased villus height, villus width, and absorptive surface area in the duodenum and jejunum, and villus width and absorptive surface area in the ileum (p < 0.05). Microbiota responses were site-dependent: alpha diversity decreased in the small intestine but was preserved in the cecum, and beta diversity separated T0 from T3 at both sites. Aeriscardovia aeriphila increased at both sites, whereas Romboutsia ilealis, Bacteroides togonis, Enterococcus cecorum, and several Streptococcus species decreased or became undetectable. Betaine combined with sodium bicarbonate improved laying performance and intestinal morphology and was associated with a marked shift in gut microbial composition under chronic tropical heat stress.

papers.title: The pecten oculi regulates pH in the bird eye
papers.abstract: The bird retina generates a dual acid load: aerobic metabolism in the outer retina produces CO2, while chronic anoxia in the inner retina yields lactic acid, raising the question of how intraocular pH homeostasis is maintained in birds. We show that chicken (Gallus gallus) vitreous pH remains close to blood pH despite these respiratory and metabolic acid-base challenges and a low non-bicarbonate buffering capacity, which is compensated by high vitreous bicarbonate. Spatial transcriptomics of eye tissue revealed enriched expression of carbonic anhydrase 2 and 4, and vacuolar-type H+-ATPase within the intraocular vascular structure, the pecten oculi. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the presence of carbonic anhydrase 2 in the pecten, suggesting an important role in ocular CO2 removal and pH regulation. Together, our findings demonstrate that bicarbonate buffering and pecten-mediated exchange of acid-base-relevant ions and metabolites act in concert to sustain retinal function under the extreme metabolic conditions of the bird eye.

papers.title: Sublethal chemical exposure predominantly reduces heat tolerance while increasing its variability in freshwater invertebrates and fish
papers.abstract: Increasing temperatures, in conjunction with widespread chemical pollution, threaten freshwater biodiversity worldwide. General patterns describing how chemical exposure affects heat tolerance have yet to be quantified beyond individual studies. Therefore we quantitatively synthesized the literature on chemical effects on the heat tolerance of freshwater fauna. We compiled heat tolerances of freshwater invertebrates and fish measured in conjunction with chemical exposure, then meta-analyzed the effect of sublethal chemical exposure on heat tolerance in terms of magnitude and variability using three-level random effects meta-analyses. We employed meta-regression to test whether these effects scale with chemical stressor intensity (acute toxicity) and differ by chemical class and taxonomic group. We found that sublethal chemical exposure consistently reduced mean heat tolerance of both fish and invertebrates with increasing toxicity across all chemical classes, with the exception of pharmaceuticals, and increased the inter-individual variation in heat tolerance measures across all chemical types. These findings imply that chemical pollution can increase freshwater species vulnerability to warming, while making their responses to acute warming harder to predict and affecting their ability to adapt. Thus, chemical pollution should be considered in assessments of freshwater species responses to ongoing climate warming.

papers.title: High-fat feeding increases graft-derived glucagon output and impairs beta-cell secretion in transplanted human islets
papers.abstract: Dysregulated glucagon secretion is central to the bihormonal disturbance that drives hyperglycemia in T2D, yet how a chronic obesogenic environment alters human alpha-cell function over time has not been directly examined. Models to specifically assess in vivo human alpha-cell function have not been possible because mouse and human glucagon are sequence-identical. We transplanted human islets (+I) into glucagon-knockout immunocompromised (GKO-NSG) mice, in which all circulating glucagon is graft-derived, and fed recipients a regular diet (RD+I) or a 60% high-fat diet (HFD+I) for 12 weeks. HFD+I recipients became obese, hyperlipidemic, hyperglycemic, and glucose intolerant, with elevated host mouse insulin indicating insulin resistance. Graft-derived human glucagon after glucose plus arginine was higher in HFD+I recipients at 4, 8, and 12 weeks. Fasting glucagon rose progressively between 4 and 12 weeks despite concurrent hyperglycemia and fasting human hyperinsulinemia, and graft endocrine composition and gross graft size were unchanged. Acute glucose-induced glucagon suppression persisted. Human beta-cells of the same grafts showed secretory dysfunction, so the impact on the two islet cell types diverged on a shared timeline. Conventional and multiplexed immunoimaging detected no accompanying changes in alpha-cell-enriched transcription factors and no change in human-derived immune, vascular, or matrix markers. Islet graft amyloid increased. In a contrasting insult, diphtheria toxin (DT) ablation of host beta-cells in GKO-NSG-DTR recipients produced severe hyperglycemia and reduced both hormones, suggesting that the direction of the human alpha-cell response may depend on the severity and nature of the insult. Inappropriate glucagon secretion is thus an early feature of the human islet response to diet-induced insulin resistance.

papers.title: L-Cystine Is a Conserved Host-Entry Signal That Activates Development in Diverse Parasitic Nematodes Through an Olfactory Receptor
papers.abstract: Soil-transmitted helminths infect over 1 billion people worldwide, yet how dormant infective larvae sense entry into a host and exit developmental arrest to establish infection remains largely unknown. Here, in the human parasite Strongyloides stercoralis, we identify L-cystine as a host signal that stimulates larval feeding and synthesis of dafachronic acid, a steroid hormone that activates DAF-12 and promotes post-infection development. A CRISPR screen of candidate receptors identified a previously uncharacterized olfactory GPCR, Ss-OR1, that is activated by L-cystine in heterologous cells and required for a normal L-cystine-induced feeding response in the parasite. Surprisingly, L-cystine also activated an OR1 homolog from the insect parasite Steinernema carpocapsae and stimulated feeding in its infective larvae. These findings identify L-cystine as a conserved host signal that activates OR1 homologs and stimulates feeding in nematodes infecting evolutionarily distant hosts.

papers.title: Variable expression of fluorescent protein expression in hematopoietic cells purified from ubiquitous reporter mice
papers.abstract: Adoptive transfer experiments (e.g. hematopoietic stem cell transplantation) are indispensable for hematology and immunology research. These assays require unambiguous detection of the transferred cells, and their offspring, to track their fates. Mice in which a fluorescent reporter protein is expressed ubiquitously in all cells are especially helpful for these fate mapping experiments as the donor cells can be easily detected using flow cytometry and confocal microscopy. We report that two commonly used reporter strains, Ubc-gfp and ROSA-mTmG, display variable expression during hematopoietic differentiation. GFP in Ubc-gfp mice labels only a fraction of megakaryocytes while TdTomato expression in ROSA-mTmG mice is progressively lost in red blood cells. We also found uneven expression of either reporter at various stages of B cell, myeloid cell or dendritic cell differentiation. Our results thus enable selection of the appropriate fluorescent reporter for identification of the hematopoietic cells of interest in adoptive transfer experiments.

papers.title: Tricuspid Valve Chordae Tendineae: Where are They, How Many are There, and What are Their Properties?
papers.abstract: Background: Tricuspid chordae play an important role in valve function. Unfortunately, they are poorly visible in clinical imaging and their mechanical properties cannot be measured noninvasively. This lack of data on chordal structure and properties limits our understanding of the tricuspid valve in general and efforts to model the valve in particular. Objectives: Our primary objective was to quantify chordal insertion patterns, structure, and mechanical properties. Our secondary objective was to test whether chordal structure and properties differed between control hearts and hearts with heart failure. Methods: We mapped chordal insertions in 25 excised human valves, measured the cross-sectional areas of 281 specimens, and conducted uniaxial tensile tests on 265 specimens from 12 of the 25 valves (eight control and four heart failure). We used mixed-effects models to assess the influence of heart failure and anatomical position. Finally, we used a hierarchical Bayesian model to represent area-dependent Ogden material parameters. Results: We found that chordal insertion density was highest at the free edge (p < 0.001), and lowest in the anterior leaflet (p < 0.001). Median cross-sectional area was 0.223 mm2, with anterior chordae the largest (p < 0.001) and septal the smallest (p < 0.001). A 10% increase in cross-sectional area was associated with 5.3% and 3.3% decreases in toe and calf stiffness, respectively. Heart failure was not associated with larger areas or higher stiffness. Conclusions: Human chordal geometry and material behavior varied with location and size. These openly shared data support assigning chordal insertions, sizes, and material properties in tricuspid valve models.

papers.title: Real-time visualization of spatial muscle activity using augmented reality improves endurance during dynamic knee extensions
papers.abstract: Purpose: High-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) quantifies the spatial distribution of muscle activity, and greater redistribution during sustained muscle contractions has been associated with longer endurance time. However, it remains unclear whether providing real-time biofeedback on the spatial distribution of muscle activity can enhance endurance. This study determined whether real-time augmented reality (AR) biofeedback on the spatial distribution of knee extensor muscle activity allowed individuals to alter the spatial activation of their muscles during dynamic contractions and improved knee extensor endurance. Methods: Fourteen healthy adults performed isokinetic knee extensions at 35% of maximal voluntary contraction torque until volitional exhaustion under two randomized conditions: with and without AR HDsEMG biofeedback. HDsEMG was recorded from the vastus lateralis and rectus femoris using a 64-electrode grid. Results: Participants completed more repetitions with biofeedback than without (p 0.05). Conclusions: AR biofeedback based on HDsEMG can improve muscular endurance while enabling individuals to modify spatial activation of their knee extensors during dynamic fatiguing exercise. These findings support the use of AR HDsEMG biofeedback as a novel tool to optimize neuromuscular function and potentially push the boundaries of athletic performance.

papers.title: Rapamycin Mitigates Branched-Chain Amino Acid Accumulation in Maple Syrup Urine Disease Mice
papers.abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is an inborn error of metabolism caused by mutations in the mitochondrial branched-chain -keto acid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) complex, resulting in toxic accumulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and their corresponding branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). This leads to poorly understood clinical features in both brain and muscle. Due to a limited understanding of MSUD pathophysiology, there is a marked paucity of effective pharmacological interventions. Here, we discovered the mTOR inhibitor, rapamycin, improves disease and extends survival in MSUD mouse models. Rapamycin treatment attenuates neuroinflammation and reduces muscle pathology. To investigate the mechanism behind these effects, we studied the accumulation of BCAAs and BCKAs. Rapamycin decreased BCAA accumulation. Overall, our work identifies rapamycin as a potential therapy for MSUD. More broadly, it suggests dysregulated mTOR signaling may drive MSUD pathobiology and advances our understanding of the mechanisms influencing leucine toxicity.

papers.title: AVF creation in mice disrupts blood flow patterns to impact vasoreactivity
papers.abstract: Maladaptive venous remodeling contributes to the high rate of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) maturation failure. Impaired vasoreactivity might impact this pathology. We created a murine AVF by anastomosing the external jugular vein to the carotid artery, establishing the AVF vein (AVF-V) and proximal (PA) and distal (DA) carotid artery. We hypothesized that endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation is impaired in the AVF-V vs. the contralateral vein (contra-V) of 5-month-old mice of both sexes 21-days post-surgery, reasoning that abrupt exposure to arterial pressure and disturbed hemodynamics promote endothelial dysfunction. Further, because magnetic resonance imaging revealed lower blood flow velocity and wall shear stress in PA vs. DA 21-days post-surgery, we hypothesized that endothelial function is compromised in PA. Whereas the thromboxane A2 receptor (TP) agonist U-46619 evoked sufficient vasocontraction in the contra-V from which subsequent vasorelaxation could be evaluated, AVF-V responsiveness was insufficient for this assessment, potentially reflecting >5-fold increases in collagen content and intima-media thickness. Consistent with our arterial hypothesis, endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation was impaired in the PA vs. DA and contralateral artery, whereas vascular smooth muscle function, cross-sectional area, collagen area, and intima-media thickness were similar among segments. Low shear stress impairs endothelial autophagy, which supports endothelial nitric oxide generation and vasodilation. Colocalized fluorescence of p-eNOSS1177 with CD31+ cells, and autophagy-related protein 3 with CD31+ cells, as well as nitric oxide bioavailability, were lower in PA vs. DA. These findings suggest that differential blood flow patterns in PA vs. DA following AVF creation may modulate endothelial autophagy, nitric oxide generation, and endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation.

papers.title: Comparative Metabolomics and Lipidomics Reveal Selective Fatty Acyl Partitioning and Metabolic Reorganization Associated with Long-Term Cold Adaptation in Euphausia superba
papers.abstract: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) inhabits the persistently cold waters of the Southern Ocean, where lipid metabolism supports membrane function and energy storage. Despite extensive characterization of euphausiid lipid classes and bulk fatty acids, fatty acyl organization across lipid pools remains poorly understood. We integrated untargeted metabolomics and lipidomics to compare whole-body biochemical profiles of E. superba and its congener E. triacantha. Metabolomics revealed differences in glycerophospholipid (GP) and glycerolipid (GL) metabolism, together with alterations in pathways associated with nucleotide metabolism, redox regulation, and lipid precursor supply. Lipidomics further revealed selective remodeling at the lipid-class and molecular-species levels rather than a global increase in lipid unsaturation. Relative to E. triacantha, E. superba showed lower relative abundances of multiple lysophospholipid classes and a higher relative abundance of cardiolipin. E. superba also showed higher relative abundances of polyunsaturated glycerophospholipids, whereas a subset of predominantly polyunsaturated triacylglycerol species showed lower relative abundances. C20:5, C22:5, and C22:6 showed higher relative abundances in the GP pool but lower relative abundances in the GL pool of E. superba. Together, these findings place selective fatty acyl partitioning within an integrated metabolic framework associated with long-term cold adaptation in E. superba.

papers.title: Photorespiration mediates plant carbon-nitrogen coordination
papers.abstract: Plant species differ widely in their sensitivity to ammonium, and legumes are generally more sensitive than cereals, yet the mechanisms behind this difference remain unclear. Photorespiration links photosynthetic carbon assimilation with nitrogen metabolism, but its response to nitrogen form has rarely been compared between species. We grew the legume Medicago truncatula, with and without rhizobia, and the cereal wild emmer wheat (Triticum dicoccoides) under nitrate or ammonium, and measured gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, leaf nitrogen, carbon isotope composition and amino acid profiles. Ammonium reduced biomass in both species, but through different leaf-level responses. In M. truncatula, ammonium increased leaf nitrogen but decreased CO2 assimilation, electron transport and photorespiratory CO2 release, lowering photosynthetic nitrogen-use efficiency. These effects were strongest in rhizobia-inoculated plants. In T. dicoccoides, ammonium increased photorespiration and photosystem II operating efficiency, photosynthesis and photosynthetic nitrogen-use efficiency were maintained, and nitrogen accumulated in asparagine and arginine-pathway amino acids. Photorespiration therefore responded in opposite directions to the same nitrogen form in the two species. We propose that sustained photorespiration helps maintain leaf carbonnitrogen coordination under ammonium, whereas its suppression marks leaf-level ammonium sensitivity, with implications for efforts to engineer photorespiration in crops.

papers.title: Confidence-Guided Machine Learning Staging of the Mouse Estrous Cycle from External Anatomical Images Reduces Cytology Burden
papers.abstract: Although the 2015 National Institutes of Health mandate to consider sex as a biological variable in preclinical studies has increased sex-inclusive study designs, many research groups continue to cite the complexity of monitoring female-specific physiology as a barrier to adoption. Central to this challenge is the murine estrous cycle, a hormonally driven process comprising four stages (proestrus, estrus, metestrus, and diestrus), each associated with distinct hormonal and cytological profiles. Current staging methods rely primarily on vaginal cytology, which requires skilled animal handling, specialized expertise in cytology observation, and considerable time, limiting their routine application outside of reproductive endocrinology. To address these barriers, we developed and evaluated a machine learning framework for estrous cycle staging based on photographs of the mouse external vaginal opening. Using 2,297 photographs from C57BL/6J and BALB/c female mice paired with concurrent cytological assessments and partitioned strictly at the animal level, we trained and evaluated three models of varying granularity: a four-stage model, a three-stage model combining metestrus and diestrus, and a two-stage binary model separating the follicular from the luteal and transitional phases. In a held-out evaluation cohort of 466 photographs from 29 unseen mice, overall classification accuracy was 47.4% (95% CI: 40.7-51.9%) for the four-stage model, 54.5% (47.6-62.9%) for the three-group model, and 69.5% (61.8-75.3%) for the binary two-group model. Misclassifications occurred predominantly between biologically adjacent stages, particularly between proestrus and estrus. Crucially, applying a calibrated confidence threshold to the two-group classifier increased accuracy to 82.8% (95% CI: 71.1-92.1%) among the 43.8% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.80, and to 92.5% (95% CI: 87.1-96.6%) among the 20.0% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.90. While external photography does not support standalone four-stage classification, confidence-guided photographic assessment offers an accessible decision-support framework to selectively triage uncertain cases for cytology and reduce the wet-lab burden of estrous monitoring in preclinical research, including cohort assembly for hormone-dependent models of genital tract infection.

papers.title: Neuritin-1 is an adipokine that sustains insulin sensitivity through adipocyte FGFR1-PPAR-gamma signaling
papers.abstract: Obesity remodels the adipose secretome, yet the adipocyte-derived signals that preserve insulin sensitivity remain incompletely defined. Here we identify neuritin (NRN1), a GPI-anchored protein, as an obesity-suppressed adipokine that protects against insulin resistance. In white adipose tissue, Nrn1 expression increases after adipocyte-specific deletion of DNA methyltransferase 3A (DNMT3A), which occupies the Nrn1 promoter. In obese mice, higher adipose DNMT3A and Nrn1 promoter methylation accompany lower Nrn1 expression, reduced NRN1 release from white adipose tissue and lower circulating NRN1. In humans, adipocyte NRN1 expression and plasma NRN1 concentrations are inversely associated with body mass index. Increasing NRN1 expression in white adipose tissue or raising circulating NRN1 improves insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis in obese mice without altering adiposity, whereas adipocyte-specific Nrn1 deletion exacerbates diet-induced insulin resistance. NRN1 enhances adipose insulin signaling and glucose uptake, raises circulating adiponectin, and restrains inflammation, adipocyte hypertrophy, and lipolysis. Mechanistically, NRN1 engages FGFR1 on adipocytes, stimulating receptor phosphorylation and downstream signaling. For cell-expressed NRN1, this association depends on native GPI-anchor processing. Pharmacological or genetic FGFR1 inhibition abrogates NRN1-induced insulin sensitization in vitro, and adipocyte-specific Fgfr1 deletion largely abolishes NRN1's adipose and systemic effects in vivo. This pathway converges on PPAR-gamma: PPAR-gamma antagonism blocks NRN1-enhanced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, whereas rosiglitazone restores this response in Nrn1-deficient adipocytes and largely corrects insulin resistance in knockout mice. Thus, NRN1 is a previously unrecognized adipokine that acts as a non-FGF signal through adipocyte FGFR1 and PPAR-gamma to preserve adipose function and systemic insulin sensitivity.

papers.title: Serum albumin restrains obesity by coordinating brown adipose thermogenic capacity with beta3-adrenergic responsiveness
papers.abstract: Obesity reflects chronic imbalance between energy storage and expenditure, yet how abundant circulating carrier proteins contribute remains poorly understood. Using constitutive and inducible albumin-deficient mice, we show that reduced circulating albumin promotes diet-induced adiposity and hepatic lipid accumulation while impairing energy expenditure, cold tolerance and stimulus-induced lipid mobilization. Recombinant mouse serum albumin (rMSA) restores thermogenic capacity and alleviates obesity, with anti-adiposity effects partly dependent on UCP1. Mechanistically, rMSA promotes brown-adipocyte thermogenic maturation through Cav1-associated Src-PI3K/AKT-mTORC1 signaling. Independently, the fatty-acid-to-albumin balance tunes beta3-adrenergic responsiveness: high fatty-acid loading shifts Cav1-associated complexes from beta3-AR toward CD36, whereas CD36 depletion restores beta3-AR association, PKA/HSL signaling and glycerol release. Glycation or oxidation impairs albumin fatty-acid binding and is associated with reduced metabolic efficacy. Thus, albumin abundance, fatty-acid loading and biochemical integrity jointly shape brown-adipose thermogenesis and obesity susceptibility.

papers.title: Rescue of KATP channel nonsense mutations using anticodon-edited transfer RNAs
papers.abstract: KATP channels composed of sulfonylurea receptor 1 (SUR1) and Kir6.2 encoded by ABCC8 and KCNJ11, respectively, play a crucial role in regulating insulin secretion. Nonsense mutations that introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) in ABCC8 and KCNJ11 disrupt KATP channel expression, resulting in congenital hyperinsulinism (HI). Currently, there is no effective non-invasive treatment for HI caused by KATP-PTCs. Anticodon-edited transfer RNAs (ACE-tRNAs), which suppress PTCs and restore full-length protein expression, have emerged as potential therapies for diseases caused by nonsense mutations. Here, we evaluate the efficacy of ACE-tRNAs to rescue the expression and function of KATP-PTCs in a heterologous COS cell expression system. In five selected SUR1-PTCs, ACE-tRNAs incorporating native amino acids at the PTC sites recovered KATP channel expression and activity. ACE-tRNALeuUGA, a highly efficient suppressor incorporating leucine at PTCs, also rescued protein expression of all five variants; however, two of the five rescued PTC variants showed impaired gating, indicating functional intolerance to Leu substitution at these positions. An exhaustive screen of the rescue effects of ACE-tRNALeu on 100 HI-associated KATP-PTCs reported to date demonstrated therapeutically meaningful functional rescue of 60 out of 92 SUR1-PTC variants and 6 out of 8 Kir6.2-PTC variants. In addition, optimized ACE-tRNASer rescues several PTCs that were unresponsive to ACE-tRNALeu, further expanding the applicability of ACE-tRNA for rescuing PTC variants. Our results demonstrate that ACE-tRNAs are effective in rescuing the expression and function of a majority of KATP PTC variants and suggest ACE-tRNAs as a promising molecular therapy for HI caused by nonsense mutations.

papers.title: Hearts in sync on a roller coaster: heart-rate responses, synchrony and psychological change in 439 amusement-park riders
papers.abstract: Background Shared intense experiences are thought to bring people closer, and synchronized physiology is a proposed reason. We examined heart rate and synchrony across ride phases, riders' response profiles, and whether these relate to changes in happiness, stress and closeness. Methods In this exploratory field study we recorded heart rate in 439 riders (418 with usable data) on 19 trains of the Balder roller coaster, Gothenburg, Sweden, and measured happiness, stress and closeness (0-10) just before and after the ride. Real pairs were compared with surrogate pairs from different trains, aligned on ride start, to separate coupling between riders from the ride's own effect. Profiles came from k-means clustering; analyses used linear mixed models. Results Heart rate rose by 15.2 beats per minute (95% CI 14.2 to 16.3) during the two-minute ride and was back at baseline within nine minutes. Heart-rate curves did not form clearly distinct types (two profiles, silhouette 0.29): riders calm in the queue rose more and stayed elevated, while riders already aroused rose less. Pairs in which both riders came with companions gained more synchrony during the ride than the surrogate benchmark (Fisher z 0.096, 95% CI 0.050 to 0.142); for pairs including a solo rider the boost was smaller and uncertain. This coupling peaked just after the ride and was gone five minutes later. Riders reported being happier (+1.3 points, Cohen's d = 0.87) and closer to the other riders on the train (+2.2 points, d = 0.70). Neither phase-specific heart-rate responses, response profile nor synchrony was associated with these changes. Conclusions A short shared thrill coupled riders' heart rates beyond what the ride alone explains, and riders felt happier and closer to others on the train afterwards, but the two ran in parallel. Without a non-riding comparison, the psychological changes cannot be attributed to the ride itself.

papers.title: Treg- and CD8-Specific PD-1 Deficiency Reveals That CD8⁺ T Cell-Intrinsic Signaling Uniquely Restrains Pressure Overload Inflammation and Heart Failure
papers.abstract: Aims: PD-1 signaling limits cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). Whether this protection depends on PD-1 signaling intrinsic to CD8 T cells or on regulation by other immune populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), remains unclear. Methods and results: Using transverse aortic constriction (TAC), we studied global PD-1-knockout (KO) mice with or without CD8 T cell depletion, CD8 T cell-specific (PD1KOCD8), and Treg-specific PD-1-KO mice. We assessed left ventricular (LV) remodeling, genomic profiles, immune infiltration, and the therapeutic impact of C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3) blockade. CD8 T cell depletion abolished TAC-induced left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy, fibrosis, and dysfunction of global PD-1-KO mice. PD1KOCD8 mice had normal baseline cardiac function but, after TAC, showed reduced survival, worse LV dysfunction and fibrosis, and greater immune cell infiltration. CD8 T cells from PD1KOCD8 mice showed increased activation and proliferation, with increased production of cytotoxic molecules, such as IFN-{gamma} and granzyme A, both at baseline and after TAC. Post-TAC transcriptomics revealed enhanced inflammatory pathways and suppressed metabolic pathways in PD1KOCD8 hearts. TAC also increased LV CXCR3+CD8+ T cell accumulation and CXCL9/CXCL10 expression in PD1KOCD8 mice. CXCR3 neutralizing antibody treatment reduced LV CD8+ T cell accumulation and attenuated cardiac dysfunction. In contrast, Treg-specific PD-1 deficiency did not alter baseline or TAC-induced cardiac remodeling. Conclusions: CD8 T cell-intrinsic PD-1 restrains TAC-induced HF, whereas Treg-intrinsic PD-1 is dispensable. CXCR3-dependent recruitment drives pathological CD8 T cell accumulation, identifying PD-1/CXCR3 axis as a key regulator of CD8 T cell-mediated cardiac injury.

papers.title: HCM-mutation G716R in β-myosin alters contractile function and responsiveness to mavacamten of human ventricular myofibrils
papers.abstract: Effects of the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) associated mutation Gly716Arg in {beta}-myosin at the sarcomeric level are unresolved. To further understand HCM-pathomechanisms in relation to modern treatment, we investigated the effect of this mutation in subcellular myofibrils isolated from HCM-patient myocardium compared to myofibrils from healthy donor hearts and tested how mavacamten influences force-related parameters. Mavacamten is a state-of-the-art myosin inhibitor aimed to treat ventricular hypercontractility of symptomatic HCM patients. Compared with donor myofibrils, patient myofibrils developed similar isometric forces, while kinetics of maximum force generation and particularly of relaxation were slower. Relaxation impairment was exacerbated when patient myofibrils were incompletely relaxed to mimic residual diastolic calcium levels. Inhibitory effects of mavacamten were dependent on force activation level and significantly less efficient in patient myofibrils. While the drug accelerated full relaxation of donor myofibrils, the slowing down effect of the mutation was not reversed by the drug in patient myofibrils. At partial relaxation, impairment was further aggravated by mavacamten in patient myofibrils. This study suggests that HCM-associated mutation G716R in {beta}-myosin does not evoke gain-of-function in human left ventricular myofibrils, and impaired relaxation could not be rescued by mavacamten. Our findings suggest that HCM-associated mutations may modulate myofibrillar sensitivity to mavacamten, providing a potential mechanistic explanation for differences in treatment response. Studies such as the present one highlight the importance of mutation-dependent sarcomeric properties in understanding variability in responses to myosin modulators and potentially informing more individualized treatment strategies.

papers.title: Modified Long-Acting UCN2 Promotes Fat Mass Loss While Preserving Skeletal Muscle Mass and Function in Mouse Models of Pharmacological Weight Loss and Sarcopenic Obesity
papers.abstract: No approved pharmacotherapy simultaneously reduces excess adiposity and preserves skeletal muscle mass and function. Such an agent would have two distinct applications: improvement of the quality of pharmacological weight loss and treatment of sarcopenic obesity. Urocortin 2 (UCN2) and its receptor corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 2 (CRHR2) are highly expressed in skeletal muscle, where they regulate hypertrophy and metabolism. Here we show that a modified long-acting acylated UCN2 peptide reduces fat mass while preserving muscle mass and enhancing function across distinct mouse models. Pair-feeding showed these effects were independent of reduced food intake. Combined with the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide or the GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist retatrutide, UCN2 produced the greatest magnitude of fat loss while preserving lean and muscle mass and increasing in vivo force production, and this gain persisted 4 weeks after dosing stopped. UCN2 increased energy expenditure, prevented the adaptive fall in expenditure caused by reduced food intake, and promoted whole-body fatty acid oxidation. In a sarcopenic obese mouse model, UCN2 reduced fat mass while increasing muscle mass, muscle function, and myofibrillar protein synthesis. These findings identify UCN2-CRHR2 signaling as a strategy to uncouple fat loss from muscle loss, both as a standalone therapy for sarcopenic obesity and as a combination partner with incretins.

papers.title: RETRO-URETERAL DELIVERY OF AAV-KP VECTORS FOR RENAL GENE TRANSFER AND THE ASSESSMENT OF TRANSGENE REABSORPTION IN THE KIDNEY
papers.abstract: Monogenic disorders cause a substantial fraction of chronic kidney disease, yet no renal gene therapy exists, partly because adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors transduce the kidney poorly after systemic delivery. Screening a barcoded library of 80 natural and chimeric AAV serotypes administered retrogradely into the mouse renal pelvis identified AAV-KP1, AAV-KP2 and AAV-KP3 as enriched in the injected kidney but not in the liver. Individual validation confirmed efficient transduction of the administered kidney, with vector genome copy numbers approaching hepatic levels, 50- to 500-fold above the contralateral kidney and far above AAV9. Using kidney-specific (KSPC) and ubiquitous (CMV) promoters, transduction was detected in collecting duct, distal convoluted tubule, proximal tubule, Bowman's capsule, interstitial cells and podocytes, with cell-type coverage depending on the promoter. Unexpectedly, GFP and mCherry protein was abundant in proximal tubules of kidneys lacking transgene mRNA, including contralateral and intravenously dosed kidneys. RNA-FISH, vector genome quantification and serum mCherry indicate that this protein derives from circulating transgene product filtered and reabsorbed by the proximal tubule rather than from local transduction. Retrograde delivery of AAV-KP capsids therefore achieves broad renal epithelial transduction, and transgene mRNA must be assessed alongside protein if kidney-tropic capsids are to be ranked reliably.

papers.title: Energetic costs of osmo- and ionoregulatory responses to desiccation and recovery in a model insect
papers.abstract: Climate change is expected to increase the frequency, duration and intensity of weather events that cause desiccation stress to small-bodied terrestrial insects. Whether a desiccation event may cause mortality depends on the time-dependent osmo- and ionoregulation responses of insects to desiccation and their recovery. Yet these responses and their associated energetic costs are not always clear for a range of mesic species. Here, we characterised the ability of house crickets (Acheta domesticus) to physiologically resist and recover from desiccation. We measured water loss from different tissues, changes in haemolymph volume and in haemolymph ion concentration as well as stored macromolecules (lipids, carbohydrates and proteins) use over a time-course of desiccation (0, 3, 6 or 18 h) and recovery with access to water and with or without access to food (18 h desiccation and 6 h recovery). During 18 h of desiccation, crickets regulated haemolymph ion concentration, avoiding hyperkalaemia and hypernatraemia, despite losing up to 14.5 and 21.1% of their body water for female and males respectively, across all body compartments. Recovery represented a distinct physiological phase to acute stress with a restoration of ion concentrations and body water with significant energetic contributions from stored macromolecules. We conclude crickets employ a general two-phase physiological strategy to withstand and recover from a short-term acute desiccation stress, establishing a physiological baseline to evaluate potential desiccation stress, and providing key insight into the time-dependency of osmoregulation and ion regulation for insects encountering fluctuating desiccation stress under climate change.

papers.title: Myeloid mDIC Deficiency Remodels Adipose Macrophages to an Efferocytosis-Associated State and Improves Metabolic Homeostasis During Obesity
papers.abstract: Obesity-associated adipose inflammation contributes to metabolic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking mitochondrial metabolism to macrophage efferocytosis remain incompletely understood. The mitochondrial dicarboxylate carrier (mDIC), encoded by SLC25A10, regulates adipocyte function, but its role in macrophages remains unclear. Here, we investigated how myeloid mDIC deficiency affects mitochondrial function, macrophage heterogeneity, and metabolic homeostasis during diet-induced obesity. We observed reduced mDIC protein expression in subcutaneous white adipose tissue from individuals with obesity, whereas palmitate increased mDIC expression in mouse and human macrophages. Myeloid mDIC deletion preserved mitochondrial respiration under palmitate stress. Single-cell RNA sequencing of adipose stromal vascular cells from high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice revealed an expanded efferocytosis-associated macrophage population and reduced proportions of inflammatory and lipid-associated macrophages. Consistently, mDIC-deficient macrophages exhibited increased Mertk expression and greater association with apoptotic cells. Pharmacological inhibition of mitochondrial ATP synthase or electron transport markedly suppressed apoptotic cell uptake, including the quenching-resistant fraction, without substantially affecting macrophage viability. In vivo, myeloid mDIC deletion attenuated HFD-induced weight gain, improved insulin sensitivity, and increased CD11c-CD206 adipose macrophage abundance, accompanied by elevated expression of alternative activation-associated markers. Together, these findings identify myeloid mDIC as an important regulator of macrophage mitochondrial function and adipose immune remodeling during obesity, suggesting a novel mechanism by which mitochondrial bioenergetics contribute to macrophage apoptotic-cell handling and metabolic homeostasis.

papers.title: Role of Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) in muscle fatigue: significance for muscle myopathies
papers.abstract: We report that Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) modulates skeletal muscle function. TLR2 ligands accelerated muscle fatigue development in isolated muscle fibers. Muscle fibers from TLR2 gene knock-out (TLR2-/-) mice were more fatigue resistant. This was not due to altered mitochondrial oxidative capacity or glycogen content. TLR2-/- muscle fibers had larger tetanic [Ca2+]i transients. Muscles from TLR2-/- mice had increased levels of Ca2+-binding proteins compared to WT muscles. Lastly, TLR2 was expressed in muscle fibers of control subjects and patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), whereas high mobility group box protein (HMGB) 1, an endogenous activator of TLR2, was only detected in the cytoplasm of muscles from IIM patients. In conclusion, TLR2 signaling regulates force production in skeletal muscle. TLR2 and its endogenous ligand, HMGB1 likely contribute to the muscle weakness in IIM and, possibly, other muscle disorders. Therapies targeted to the TLR2 signaling pathway may counteract pathological muscle weakness.

papers.title: Posterior Staphyloma-associated vitreous proteomic remodeling in high myopia
papers.abstract: Posterior staphyloma is a hallmark of pathologic myopia, but the cellular and molecular changes of the overlying retina remain poorly understood. We combined the histopathology of human eyes with posterior staphyloma with label-free proteomics of vitreous from non-myopic eyes (n = 4) and highly myopic eyes without (n = 3) or with posterior staphyloma (n = 7) and measured soluble vitreous iron in an independent series of 31 eyes. In the staphyloma, the retina collapsed at the transition zones into a vimentin- and GFAP-positive glial scar containing Iba1-positive microglia, with iron deposits, increased ferritin and disorganized scleral collagen. The vitreous proteome was not globally altered, but protein modules defined a priori to mirror these lesions revealed an activation of the classical complement pathway and an increased ferritin-to-transferrin ratio, both specific to staphylomatous eyes, whereas neuron- and photoreceptor-derived proteins were already decreased in highly myopic eyes without staphyloma. Soluble vitreous iron was lower in staphylomatous eyes than in non-myopic eyes and in highly myopic eyes without staphyloma, independently of total protein content. These findings suggest that complement activation and iron sequestration characterize the retinal degeneration associated with posterior staphyloma, and that the vitreous provides a window on these processes.

papers.title: The cost of stressing the royal family: parental glucocorticoid exposure has delayed adverse effects on chick physiology and survival in king penguins
papers.abstract: When exposed to stressful environmental conditions, adults of long-lived species may favour self-maintenance at the expense of reproductive investment. In breeding king penguins (Aptenodytes patagonicus), we previously showed that prolonged glucocorticoid hormone exposure during early breeding resulted in surprisingly little effect on parental self-maintenance. Here, we investigate whether the potential costs of this experimental stressor could be transferred to offspring through altered parental care, negatively affecting their growth, physiology and survival. We exposed parents to a ca. 1-month elevation in corticosterone and monitored parental investment and offspring performance over one year, from incubation to fledging. Corticosterone-treated parents exhibited reduced prolactin levels and spent less time at sea, highlighting alterations in both endocrine and behavioural processes supporting parental investment. Yet, parental care behaviour, hatching success and chick body mass/size were not significantly impacted. Major delayed costs of the parental treatment were however evident, as chicks from corticosterone-treated parents exhibited accelerated postnatal telomere shortening and faced nearly twice the mortality hazard of chicks from placebo-treated parents. By revealing the hidden reproductive costs of apparent parental resilience, our study challenges how we assess the consequences of environmental stressors in long-lived species, particularly when their effects only emerge long after exposure.

papers.title: Determination of mitochondrial matrix pH during ischemia-reperfusion injury in the isolated mouse heart using a genetically encoded fluorescent sensor
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial matrix pH (pHmtx) regulates cellular energetics, metabolite flux, and ion transport. Despite its importance in cellular energy metabolism and disease, pHmtx remains difficult to measure in the intact heart because pH-sensitive dyes are challenging to selectively target to the mitochondrial matrix. Changes in intracellular pH during cardiac ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) are significant and understanding pHmtx dynamics I/R would provide insight into mechanisms of injury. To overcome uncertainties associated with intracellular dye distribution, the pH-sensitive green fluorescent protein SypHer3 was stably expressed in the mitochondrial matrix of the adult mouse heart using adeno-associated virus (AAV). The isolated perfused heart was subjected to global no-flow ischemia, followed by reperfusion and SypHer3 fluorescence measured using an optical integrating sphere. Calibration of SypHer3 fluorescence fold-change against pH in isolated mitochondria enabled pHmtx quantification from SypHer3 fluorescence in the intact heart, based on an assigned starting pH of 7.47. We found that pHmtx decreased from 7.45 {+/-} 0.01 (n=5) during normoxia to 6.61 {+/-} 0.20 (n=5) after 20 minutes of ischemia, and reached 7.16 {+/-} 0.01 (n=5) within 1 minute of reperfusion. In paired experiments, we measured relative changes in mitochondrial Ca2+ (Ca2+m) in the isolated heart during I/R using the genetically encoded, mitochondrial-targeted Ca2+ sensor R-GECO1. Because R-GECO1 fluorescence is pH-sensitive, quantification of pHmtx is required to correct R-GECO1 fluorescence for pH-dependent effects. With correction for pH, R-GECO1 fluorescence increased 1.77 {+/-} 0.40-fold (n=7) within 20 minutes of ischemia and returned to baseline within the first minute of reperfusion, consistent with an increase in Ca2+m during ischemia that reversed upon reperfusion. In summary, we developed a fluorescence approach for measuring pHmtx, a key determinant of mitochondrial energetics and ion transport, in the isolated perfused mouse heart, providing time resolved quantitative estimates of pHmtx during I/R. Furthermore, this work expands the application of fluorescent sensors for interrogating mitochondrial physiology in the intact heart by providing a framework for accounting for pH-dependent effects on probe fluorescence.

papers.title: Distinct calcium, sodium, and water programs characterize mouse and human connecting tubule
papers.abstract: The kidney connecting tubule lies between the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct. Even though short, it plays a key role in regulating calcium, sodium, and potassium excretion and water balance in health and disease. In rodents and humans, transitions between distal segments are gradual, making the assignment of functional properties to cell types difficult. To address this, we enriched mouse kidney distal tubule cells prior to performing single nucleus RNA-sequencing. Connecting tubule cells separated into three clusters, one expressed genes that are relevant to calcium transport, while another expressed genes that are relevant to water transport. The third was intermediate between the other two. While genes for electrogenic sodium transport were expressed throughout the connecting tubule, Hsd11b2, the gene responsible for aldosterone-responsiveness, was expressed primarily by the distal cluster. Immunocytochemistry confirmed the separation of calcium and water transport pathways and spatial transcriptomics confirmed the linear organization of this segment. Human transcriptomic data showed similar gene separation. The results show that rodent and human connecting tubules separate calcium and water transport, thereby limiting tubule fluid calcium accumulation. They also restrict aldosterone action to segments that are responsive to arginine vasopressin to maintain sodium homeostasis during antidiuresis.
